description: Target the compute-bound large conv shapes (k=16/32, ch=128) where we sit 4.7x behind #1's conv2d_fft.py. Replace spatial cuDNN convolution with FFT-based convolution: zero-pad input and kernel to a common size, batched cuFFT R2C forward on both, complex pointwise multiply-accumulate across input channels (a per-output-channel batched complex GEMM), then C2R inverse, crop the valid region. Cache cuFFT plans per shape. FFT cost is O(N^2 log N) vs O(N^2 K^2), a huge win at k=16/32.

Attack the cuDNN layout-conversion overhead: the baseline profile shows an nhwcToNchwKernel transpose stealing time around the conv. Force a single fused implicit-GEMM path that stays in one layout end-to-end: try channels_last throughout, cudnnFind the best algo per shape, or drop to a CUTLASS implicit-GEMM conv. Eliminate the transpose kernels and avoid the im2col materialization on the k=16 shapes. Keep CUDA-graph capture per shape.

FFT is blocked: the harness checks against EXACT fp32 F.conv2d (atol=1e-3) and the baseline im2col+fp32-bmm passes only because it reproduces cuDNN's fp32 reduction rounding. Pursue a correctness-safe SPEED win: explicit im2col + cuBLAS SGEMM with TF32 OFF (cublasSetMathMode default, no tensor cores) for the big k=16/32 ch=128 shapes, fusing the per-batch GEMM and avoiding cuDNN's nhwcToNchw transpose. Tune tile/layout and graph-capture per shape; must stay bit-close to fp32 reference. Beat 4745us geomean.

The prior TF32-WMMA attempt failed the exact-fp32 atol=1e-3 check. Stay in fp32 and beat cuDNN's default algo: exhaustively benchmark all cuDNN forward conv algorithms per shape (cudnnFindConvolutionForwardAlgorithmEx or torch cudnn.benchmark=True warmed thoroughly), try channels_last end-to-end to kill the nhwcToNchwKernel transpose seen in the baseline profile, and select per-shape the fastest fp32-accurate algo. Graph-capture each shape. Target the k=16/32 ch=128 shapes; keep all shapes correct.
